title: Reduce shared object churn and hot-path kernel cache
creator: Avery Chen
description: Observed intermittent operator cold-starts and increased P95 latencies in mixed-model fleets. Root cause analysis shows excessive shared-object (so) load/unload churn and frequent kernel symbol re-resolution on hot inference paths when model variants or quantized kernels are swapped. This ticket consolidates a lightweight kernel cache and reduces shared-object churn by introducing a bounded in-memory SO handle cache, canonicalized symbol lookup, and an eviction policy tuned for inference hot paths. Goal is to reduce cold-start token latency variance, lower OS-level page faults during rollouts, and make live rollback safer by insulating callers from transient symbol unavailability.
design_notes: Approach: add a runtime-level SO handle cache (LRU with TTL) keyed by (so-BLOB-hash, load-flags, device-arch). Provide an explicit canonical symbol resolver that caches resolved function pointers with ABI-stability checks (signature hash). Introduce a short-lived 'symbol-grace' window during canary deploys so new bundles can register symbols before traffic hits them. Prefer non-invasive changes: keep public kernel adapter APIs unchanged, implement cache behind a feature gate 'so_hot_cache'. Avoid heavy changes to loader plumbing; instead wrap current loader with a cache facade. Measure before/after with synthetic startup/rollout benchmarks and in-cluster canary traffic. Rollout plan: feature-flag -> canary on small fleet -> monitor telemetry -> global enable. Non-goals: reworking cutlass/triton internals or entire plugin ABI redesign.
acceptance_criteria: Reduce average cold-start kernel lookup time by >= 30% in benchmark harness for mixed-model scenarios
P95 token latency variance reduced by >= 15% across canary fleet during model rollouts
No increase in resident memory > 5% on GPU-serving nodes under steady-state traffic
Symbol resolution includes ABI signature validation; mismatches logged and flagged (no silent resolution)
Automated unit tests and integration tests for eviction, TTL, and ABI-mismatch behavior merged
Canary rollout demonstrates zero 5xx regressions attributable to loader changes

Post-mortem template and checklist for any regressions during canary (All)
risks: Cache introduces stale symbol pointer risk if underlying SO is replaced out-of-band; mitigated by signature checks and TTL
Memory pressure on nodes if cache grows uncontrolled; mitigated by bounded LRU and metrics-driven defaults
Edge-case: different driver/cuda combinations may produce incompatible symbol layouts; add per-device-arch keying and guardrails
Potential for subtle ABI mismatches causing silent corruption — must err on side of fail-fast and log loudly
comments: 2026-02-14 - Avery Chen: Initial triage discovered repeated dlopen/dlclose spikes correlated with model swap events. Captured perf profile and pfault samples in eu-west-1. Decided to prototype facade cache first to measure impact.

2026-02-20 - Ramesh Patel: Prototype implemented. Simple LRU with TTL=300s passes unit tests. Microbenchmarks show 42% reduction in symbol lookup time for synthetic workloads. Pushed PR for early review.
2026-02-23 - Lina Moreno (SRE): Bench harness updated to simulate 200-model mixed fleet. Observed resident set increase ~3% with cache enabled at default size 512 entries. No CPU regressions.

2026-03-01 - Design review (Avery, Ramesh, Lina, Marco): Agreed to add ABI signature hash on first resolution, persist in cache entry. On mismatch, log and return loader failure. Decided not to attempt hot-swap of cached pointers; instead rely on TTL and explicit invalidation API.

2026-03-05 - QA (Nina Gupta): Integration test simulating canary rollback failing intermittently; root cause: test harness was reusing mem-mapped files causing stale handles. Fixed test to force explicit dlclose between cycles. Re-running tests.

2026-03-10 - Ramesh Patel: Preparing canary rollout in eu-west-1 tomorrow. Runbook drafted and docs published. Metrics queries for 'so_cache_hits' and 'so_cache_evictions' added. Will monitor p95_token_latency and pfault_count closely.
